verses.text: For di third year of di reign of Jehoiakim king of Judah, Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon come to Jerusalem and besiege am.

Di Lord give Jehoiakim king of Judah into im hand, with part of di vessels of di house of God. Dem carry dem into di land of Shinar to di house of im god, and e bring di vessels into di treasure house of im god.
Di king speak to Ashpenaz di master of im eunuchs, say make e bring some of di children of Israel, even of di royal offspring and of di nobles,

young men wey no get blemish, but good looking, and skilful in all wisdom, and endowed with knowledge, and understanding science, and wey get ability to stand for di king palace. E tell am to teach dem di literature and language of di Chaldeans.
Di king appoint for dem daily portion of di king food, and of di wine wey e drink, and say make dem nourish dem three years, so that at di end of dem dem go stand before di king.
Among dem, of di children of Judah, na Daniel, Hananiah, Mishael, and Azariah.
Di prince of di eunuchs give names to dem. E give Daniel di name Belteshazzar, and Hananiah Shadrach, and Mishael Meshach, and Azariah Abednego.
But Daniel purpose for im heart say e no go defile imself with di king food, nor with di wine wey e drink. Therefore e ask di prince of di eunuchs say e no go defile imself.
Now God make Daniel find favour and compassion for di sight of di prince of di eunuchs.

Di prince of di eunuchs talk to Daniel, “I dey fear my lord di king, wey don appoint your food and your drink. Why e go see your faces sadder pass di young men wey dey your age? Den una go endanger my head with di king.”
Den Daniel talk to di steward wey di prince of di eunuchs don set over Daniel, Hananiah, Mishael, and Azariah,
“Test your servants, I beg you, ten days, and make dem give us vegetables to eat and water to drink.
Den make our appearance dey looked on before you, and di appearance of di young men wey eat di king food. As you see, deal with your servants.”
So e listen to dem for dis matter, and test dem ten days.
At di end of ten days dem appearance dey better and fatter for flesh pass all di young men wey eat di king food.
So di steward take away dem food, and di wine wey dem for drink, and give dem vegetables.
As for dis four young men, God give dem knowledge and skill in all literature and wisdom. Daniel get understanding in all visions and dreams.
At di end of di days wey di king don appoint for dem to dey brought in, di prince of di eunuchs bring dem in before Nebuchadnezzar.
Di king talk with dem, and among dem all dey found none like Daniel, Hananiah, Mishael, and Azariah. So dem stand before di king.
For every matter of wisdom and understanding, wey di king ask dem, e find dem ten times better pass all di magicians and enchanters wey dey inside all im realm.
Daniel continue even to di first year of King Cyrus.
For di second year of di reign of Nebuchadnezzar, Nebuchadnezzar dream dreams. Im spirit dey troubled, and im sleep go from am.
Den di king command to call di magicians, and di enchanters, and di sorcerers, and di Chaldeans, to tell di king im dreams. So dem come and stand before di king.
Di king talk to dem, “I don dream dream, and my spirit dey troubled to know di dream.”
Den di Chaldeans talk to di king for Aramaic, “King, live forever! Tell your servants di dream, and we go show di interpretation.”
Di king answer di Chaldeans, “Di thing don go from me. If una no make known to me di dream and di interpretation of am, una go dey cut in pieces, and una houses go dey made dunghill.
But if una show di dream and di interpretation of am, una go receive from me gifts and rewards and great honour. Therefore show me di dream and di interpretation of am.”
Dem answer di second time, “Make di king tell im servants di dream, and we go show di interpretation.”
Di king answer, “I know certainly say una dey buy time, because una see say di thing don go from me.

But if una no make known to me di dream, only one law dey for una. Because una don prepare lying and corrupt words to speak before me, until di time don change. Therefore tell me di dream, and I go know say una fit show me di interpretation of am.”
Di Chaldeans answer before di king, “No man dey upon di earth wey fit show di king matter. Therefore no king, lord, or ruler don ever ask such thing of any magician, enchanter, or Chaldean.
Di thing wey di king dey ask dey difficult, and no other fit show am before di king, except di gods, wey im dwelling no dey with flesh.”
For dis cause di king dey angry and very furious, and command to destroy all di wise men of Babylon.
So di decree go out, and di wise men dey about to dey killed. Dem seek Daniel and im companions to kill dem.
Den Daniel answer with counsel and wisdom to Arioch di captain of di king guard, wey don go out to kill di wise men of Babylon.
E answer Arioch di king captain, “Why di decree dey so urgent from di king?” Den Arioch make di thing known to Daniel.
Daniel go in, and ask di king say e go give am time, and e go show di king di interpretation.
Den Daniel go to im house, and make di thing known to Hananiah, Mishael, and Azariah, im companions,
say dem go seek mercies from di God of heaven concerning dis secret, so that Daniel and im companions no go perish with di rest of di wise men of Babylon.
Den di secret dey revealed to Daniel for night vision. Den Daniel bless di God of heaven.
Daniel answer, “Blessed be di name of God forever and ever, because wisdom and might na im own.
E change di times and di seasons. E remove kings, and set up kings. E give wisdom to di wise, and knowledge to dem wey get understanding.
E reveal deep and secret things. E know wetin dey for darkness, and light dey dwell with am.
I thank you, and praise you, you God of my fathers, wey don give me wisdom and might, and don now make known to me wetin we ask of you, because you don make known to us di king matter.”

Therefore Daniel go in to Arioch, whom di king don appoint to destroy di wise men of Babylon. E go and talk to am like dis: “No destroy di wise men of Babylon. Bring me in before di king, and I go show di king di interpretation.”
Den Arioch bring Daniel in before di king in haste, and talk to am like dis: “I don find one man of di captives of Judah, wey go make known to di king di interpretation.”
Di king answer Daniel, wey im name na Belteshazzar, “You fit make known to me di dream wey I don see, and di interpretation of am?”
Daniel answer before di king, and talk, “Di secret wey di king don ask, di wise men, di enchanters, di magicians, and di diviners no fit show to di king.
But God dey for heaven wey reveal secrets, and e don make known to King Nebuchadnezzar wetin go be for di latter days. Your dream and di visions of your head upon your bed na dis:
As for you, king, your thoughts come into your mind upon your bed, wetin go come to pass hereafter. Im wey reveal secrets don make known to you wetin go happen.

But as for me, dis secret no dey revealed to me for any wisdom wey I get more pass any living, but to di intent say di interpretation go dey made known to di king, and say you go know di thoughts of your heart.
You, king, see, and look, great image. Dis image, wey dey mighty, and im brightness dey excellent, stand before you. Im appearance dey terrible.
As for dis image, im head na fine gold, im breast and im arms of silver, im belly and im thighs of bronze,
im legs of iron, im feet part of iron and part of clay.
You watch until stone dey cut out without hands, wey strike di image upon im feet wey be iron and clay, and break dem in pieces.

Den di iron, di clay, di bronze, di silver, and di gold dey broken in pieces together, and become like chaff of di summer threshing floors. Di wind carry dem away, so that no place dey found for dem. But di stone wey strike di image become great mountain, and fill di whole earth.
Dis na di dream. We go tell di interpretation of am before di king.
You, king, na king of kings, to whom di God of heaven don give di kingdom, di power, di strength, and di glory.
Wherever di children of men dwell, di animals of di field and di birds of di sky, e don give dem into your hand, and don make you ruler over dem all. You na di head of gold.
After you go rise another kingdom wey go dey inferior to you, and another third kingdom of bronze, wey go rule over all di earth.
Di fourth kingdom go be strong like iron, because iron break in pieces and subdue all things. As iron wey crush all dis, e go break in pieces and crush.
Whereas you see di feet and toes, part of potter clay and part of iron, di kingdom go dey divided, but some of di strength of iron go dey inside am, as you see di iron mixed with miry clay.
As di toes of di feet na part of iron and part of clay, so di kingdom go be partly strong, and partly broken.
Whereas you see iron mixed with miry clay, dem go mix demselves with di seed of men, but dem no go hold together, even as iron no dey mix with clay.

For di days of dose kings di God of heaven go set up kingdom wey no go ever dey destroyed, nor di kingdom go dey left to another people. E go break in pieces and consume all dis kingdoms, and e go stand forever.

Because you see say stone dey cut out of di mountain without hands, and say e break in pieces di iron, di bronze, di clay, di silver, and di gold, di great God don make known to di king wetin go come to pass hereafter. Di dream dey certain, and di interpretation of am dey sure.”
Den King Nebuchadnezzar fall on im face, and worship Daniel, and command say dem go offer offering and incense to am.
Di king answer Daniel, and talk, “Of truth, your God na God of gods, and Lord of kings, and revealer of secrets, seeing say you fit reveal dis secret.”
Den di king make Daniel great, and give am many great gifts, and make am ruler over di whole province of Babylon, and chief governor over all di wise men of Babylon.
Daniel ask di king, and e appoint Shadrach, Meshach, and Abednego over di affairs of di province of Babylon, but Daniel dey for di king gate.
Nebuchadnezzar di king make image of gold, wey im height na 60 cubits, and im width six cubits. E set am up for di plain of Dura, for di province of Babylon.

Den Nebuchadnezzar di king send to gather together di satraps, di deputies, and di governors, di counselors, di treasurers, di judges, di magistrates, and all di rulers of di provinces, to come to di dedication of di image wey Nebuchadnezzar di king don set up.

Den di satraps, di deputies, and di governors, di counselors, di treasurers, di judges, di magistrates, and all di rulers of di provinces dey gathered together to di dedication of di image wey Nebuchadnezzar di king don set up. Dem stand before di image wey Nebuchadnezzar don set up.
Den di herald cry aloud, “To una e dey commanded, peoples, nations, and languages,
say for di time wey una hear di sound of di horn, flute, zither, lyre, harp, pipe, and all kinds of music, una go fall down and worship di golden image wey Nebuchadnezzar di king don set up.
Whoever no fall down and worship go dey cast, di same hour, into di middle of burning fiery furnace.”

Therefore, at dat time, when all di peoples hear di sound of di horn, flute, zither, lyre, harp, and all kinds of music, all di peoples, nations, and languages fall down and worship di golden image wey Nebuchadnezzar di king don set up.
Therefore at dat time certain Chaldeans come near, and accuse di Jews.
Dem speak and talk to Nebuchadnezzar di king, “King, live forever.
You, king, don make decree, say every man wey hear di sound of di horn, flute, zither, lyre, harp, and pipe, and all kinds of music, go fall down and worship di golden image.
Whoever no fall down and worship go dey cast into di middle of burning fiery furnace.

Certain Jews dey wey you don set over di affairs of di province of Babylon: Shadrach, Meshach, and Abednego. Dis men, king, no pay attention to you. Dem no serve your gods, nor worship di golden image wey you don set up.”
Den Nebuchadnezzar for rage and fury command to bring Shadrach, Meshach, and Abednego. Den dem bring dis men before di king.
Nebuchadnezzar speak and talk to dem, “Na on purpose, Shadrach, Meshach, and Abednego, say una no serve my gods, nor worship di golden image wey I don set up?

Now if una dey ready, say at di time wey una hear di sound of di horn, flute, zither, lyre, harp, and pipe, and all kinds of music, una go fall down and worship di image wey I don make, well. But if una no worship, una go dey cast di same hour into di middle of burning fiery furnace. Who be di god wey go deliver una out of my hands?”
Shadrach, Meshach, and Abednego answer di king, “Nebuchadnezzar, we no need to answer you for dis matter.
If e dey so, our God whom we serve fit deliver us from di burning fiery furnace. E go deliver us out of your hand, king.
But if no, make e dey known to you, king, say we no go serve your gods, nor worship di golden image wey you don set up.”

Den Nebuchadnezzar dey full of fury, and di appearance of im face change against Shadrach, Meshach, and Abednego. E speak, and command say dem go heat di furnace seven times more pass wetin dem suppose heat am.
E command certain mighty men wey dey im army to bind Shadrach, Meshach, and Abednego, and to cast dem into di burning fiery furnace.
Den dem bind dis men in dem trousers, dem tunics, and dem turbans, and dem other garments, and dem cast dem into di middle of di burning fiery furnace.
Therefore because di king command dey urgent, and di furnace dey exceeding hot, di flame of di fire kill dem men wey take up Shadrach, Meshach, and Abednego.
Dis three men, Shadrach, Meshach, and Abednego, fall down bound into di middle of di burning fiery furnace.
Den Nebuchadnezzar di king dey astonished, and rise up in haste. E speak and talk to im counselors, “We no cast three men bound into di middle of di fire?” Dem answer di king, “True, king.”
E answer, “Look! I see four men loose, walking for di middle of di fire, and dem no get hurt. Di appearance of di fourth dey like son of di gods.”

Den Nebuchadnezzar come near to di mouth of di burning fiery furnace. E speak and talk, “Shadrach, Meshach, and Abednego, una servants of di Most High God, come out, and come here!” Den Shadrach, Meshach, and Abednego come out of di middle of di fire.

Di satraps, di deputies, and di governors, and di king counselors gather together, and see dis men, say di fire no get power on dem bodies. Di hair of dem head no dey singed, neither dem trousers dey changed, neither di smell of fire don pass on dem.

Nebuchadnezzar speak and talk, “Blessed be di God of Shadrach, Meshach, and Abednego, wey don send im angel, and deliver im servants wey trust for am, and don change di king word, and yield dem bodies, say dem no go serve nor worship any god except dem own God.

Therefore I make decree say every people, nation, and language wey speak anything amiss against di God of Shadrach, Meshach, and Abednego go dey cut in pieces, and dem houses go dey made dunghill, because no other god dey wey fit deliver after dis manner.”
Den di king promote Shadrach, Meshach, and Abednego for di province of Babylon.
Nebuchadnezzar di king, to all di peoples, nations, and languages wey dwell for all di earth: Peace dey multiply to una.
E seem good to me to show di signs and wonders wey di Most High God don work toward me.
How great na im signs! How mighty na im wonders! Im kingdom na everlasting kingdom, and im dominion dey from generation to generation.
I, Nebuchadnezzar, dey at ease for my house, and flourishing for my palace.
I see dream wey make me afraid. Di thoughts upon my bed and di visions of my head trouble me.
So I make decree to bring all di wise men of Babylon in before me, so that dem go make known to me di interpretation of di dream.
Den di magicians, di enchanters, di Chaldeans, and di diviners come in. I tell di dream before dem, but dem no make known to me di interpretation.
But at last Daniel come in before me, wey im name na Belteshazzar, according to di name of my god, and for whom di spirit of di holy gods dey. I tell di dream before am, say,

“Belteshazzar, master of di magicians, because I know say di spirit of di holy gods dey inside you, and no secret trouble you, tell me di visions of my dream wey I don see, and di interpretation of am.
Dis na di visions of my head upon my bed: I look, and see, tree for di middle of di earth, and im height dey great.
Di tree grow, and dey strong, and im height reach to heaven, and im sight to di end of all di earth.
Im leaves dey beautiful, and im fruit plenty, and for am dey food for all. Di animals of di field get shadow under am, and di birds of di sky dwell for im branches, and all flesh dey fed from am.
I see for di visions of my head upon my bed, and see, watcher and holy one come down from heaven.
E cry aloud, and talk like dis: ‘Cut down di tree, and cut off im branches. Shake off im leaves, and scatter im fruit. Make di animals get away from under am, and di birds from im branches.

Nevertheless leave di stump of im roots for di earth, even with band of iron and bronze, for di tender grass of di field. Make am dey wet with di dew of heaven, and make im portion dey with di animals for di grass of di earth.
Make im heart dey changed from man own, and make beast heart dey given to am, and make seven times pass over am.

Di sentence dey by di decree of di watchers, and di demand by di word of di holy ones, to di intent say di living go know say di Most High rule for di kingdom of men, and give am to whomever e wish, and set up over am di lowest of men.’

I, King Nebuchadnezzar, don see dis dream. You, Belteshazzar, declare di interpretation, because all di wise men of my kingdom no fit make known to me di interpretation. But you fit, because di spirit of di holy gods dey inside you.”

Den Daniel, wey im name na Belteshazzar, dey astonished for one hour, and im thoughts trouble am. Di king speak, and talk, “Belteshazzar, no make di dream or di interpretation trouble you.” Belteshazzar answer, “My lord, make di dream dey for dem wey hate you, and di interpretation for your enemies.
Di tree wey you see, wey grow, and dey strong, wey im height reach to heaven, and im sight to all di earth,
wey im leaves dey beautiful, and im fruit plenty, and for am dey food for all, under am di animals of di field dwell, and upon im branches di birds of di sky get dem habitation,
na you, king, wey grow and dey strong, because your greatness don grow, and reach to heaven, and your dominion to di end of di earth.

Whereas di king see watcher and holy one come down from heaven, and talk, ‘Cut down di tree, and destroy am. Nevertheless leave di stump of im roots for di earth, even with band of iron and bronze, for di tender grass of di field. Make am dey wet with di dew of heaven, and make im portion dey with di animals of di field, until seven times pass over am,’
dis na di interpretation, king, and dis na di decree of di Most High, wey don come on my lord di king:

dat dem go drive you from men, and your dwelling go be with di animals of di field. Dem go make you eat grass like oxen, and dem go wet you with di dew of heaven, and seven times go pass over you, until you know say di Most High rule for di kingdom of men, and give am to whomever e wish.
Whereas dem command to leave di stump of di roots of di tree, your kingdom go dey sure to you, after dat you don know say Heaven dey rule.
Therefore, king, make my counsel dey acceptable to you, and break off your sins by righteousness, and your iniquities by showing mercy to di poor. Maybe e go be lengthening of your tranquility.”
All dis come on di king Nebuchadnezzar.
At di end of 12 months e dey waka for di royal palace of Babylon.
Di king speak and talk, “No be dis na great Babylon, wey I don build for di royal house, by di might of my power and for di glory of my majesty?”
While di word dey still for di king mouth, voice fall from heaven: “King Nebuchadnezzar, to you e dey spoken: Di kingdom don depart from you.

Dem go drive you from men, and your dwelling go be with di animals of di field. Dem go make you eat grass like oxen, and seven times go pass over you, until you know say di Most High rule for di kingdom of men, and give am to whomever e wish.”

Di same hour di thing dey fulfilled upon Nebuchadnezzar. E dey driven from men, and ate grass like oxen, and im body dey wet with di dew of heaven, until im hair grow like eagles feathers, and im nails like birds claws.

At di end of di days, I, Nebuchadnezzar, lift up my eyes to heaven, and my understanding return to me, and I bless di Most High, and I praise and honour am wey live forever, whose dominion na everlasting dominion, and im kingdom dey from generation to generation.

All di inhabitants of di earth dey regarded as nothing, and e do according to im will among di army of heaven and among di inhabitants of di earth. None fit stay im hand, or talk to am, “Wetin you don do?”

For di same time my understanding return to me, and for di glory of my kingdom, my majesty and brightness return to me. My counselors and my lords seek me, and I dey established for my kingdom, and excellent greatness dey added to me.
Now I, Nebuchadnezzar, praise and extol and honour di King of heaven, because all im works dey truth, and im ways justice. Dem wey waka for pride e dey able to humble.
Belshazzar di king make great feast for 1,000 of im lords, and drink wine before di 1,000.

Belshazzar, while e dey taste di wine, command say dem go bring di golden and silver vessels wey Nebuchadnezzar im father don take out of di temple wey dey Jerusalem, so that di king and im lords, im wives and im concubines, go drink from dem.
Den dem bring di golden vessels wey dem take out of di temple of di house of God wey dey Jerusalem, and di king and im lords, im wives and im concubines, drink from dem.
Dem drink wine, and praise di gods of gold, and of silver, of bronze, of iron, of wood, and of stone.
For di same hour fingers of man hand come out, and write opposite di lampstand upon di plaster of di wall of di king palace. Di king see di part of di hand wey write.
Den di king countenance change, and im thoughts trouble am, so that di joints of im loins loose, and im knees knock one against another.

Di king cry aloud to bring in di enchanters, di Chaldeans, and di diviners. Di king speak and talk to di wise men of Babylon, “Whoever read dis writing, and show me di interpretation, go dey clothed with purple, and get chain of gold about im neck, and go be di third ruler for di kingdom.”
Den all di king wise men come in, but dem no fit read di writing, nor make known to di king di interpretation.
Den King Belshazzar dey greatly troubled, and im countenance dey changed for am, and im lords dey perplexed.

Di queen, because of di words of di king and im lords, come into di banquet house. Di queen speak and talk, “King, live forever. No make your thoughts trouble you, nor make your countenance dey changed.

Man dey for your kingdom wey di spirit of di holy gods dey inside am. For di days of your father, light and understanding and wisdom, like di wisdom of di gods, dey found for am. King Nebuchadnezzar your father, your father di king, make am master of di magicians, enchanters, Chaldeans, and diviners,

because excellent spirit, and knowledge, and understanding, interpreting of dreams, and showing of riddles, and solving of knots, dey found for dis Daniel, whom di king name Belteshazzar. Now make Daniel dey called, and e go show di interpretation.”
Den Daniel dey brought in before di king. Di king speak and talk to Daniel, “Na you be Daniel, wey be one of di captives of Judah, wey di king my father bring out of Judah?
I don hear of you say di spirit of di gods dey inside you, and say light and understanding and excellent wisdom dey found for you.
Now di wise men, di enchanters, don dey brought in before me, say dem go read dis writing, and make known to me di interpretation of am, but dem no fit show di interpretation of di matter.

But I don hear of you say you fit give interpretations, and solve knots. Now if you fit read di writing, and make known to me di interpretation of am, you go dey clothed with purple, and get chain of gold about your neck, and go be di third ruler for di kingdom.”
Den Daniel answer before di king, “Make your gifts dey for yourself, and give your rewards to another. Nevertheless I go read di writing to di king, and make known to am di interpretation.
You, king, di Most High God give Nebuchadnezzar your father di kingdom, and greatness, and glory, and majesty.

Because of di greatness wey e give am, all di peoples, nations, and languages tremble and fear before am. Whom e want, e kill, and whom e want, e keep alive. Whom e want, e raise up, and whom e want, e put down.
But when im heart dey lifted up, and im spirit hardened so that e deal proudly, e dey deposed from im kingly throne, and dem take im glory from am.

E dey driven from di sons of men, and im heart dey made like di animals, and im dwelling dey with di wild donkeys. Dem feed am with grass like oxen, and im body dey wet with di dew of heaven, until e know say di Most High God rule for di kingdom of men, and say e appoint over am whomever e want.
You im son, Belshazzar, no humble your heart, though you know all dis,

but you don lift up yourself against di Lord of heaven. Dem don bring di vessels of im house before you, and you, and your lords, your wives, and your concubines, don drink wine from dem. You don praise di gods of silver, and gold, of bronze, iron, wood, and stone, wey no see, nor hear, nor know. But di God in whose hand your breath dey, and whose na all your ways, you no glorify.
Den di part of di hand dey sent from am, and dis writing dey inscribed.
Dis na di writing wey dey inscribed: MENE, MENE, TEKEL, PARSIN.
Dis na di interpretation of di thing: MENE: God don number your kingdom, and finish am.
TEKEL: you dey weighed for di balances, and found lacking.
PERES: your kingdom dey divided, and given to di Medes and Persians.”
Den dem command, and dem clothe Daniel with purple, and put chain of gold about im neck, and make proclamation concerning am, say e go be di third ruler for di kingdom.
For dat night Belshazzar di Chaldean king dey killed.
Darius di Mede receive di kingdom, being about 62 years old.
E please Darius to set over di kingdom 120 satraps, wey go dey throughout di whole kingdom,
and over dem three presidents (of whom Daniel na one), so that di satraps go give account to dem, and di king go suffer no loss.
Den dis Daniel distinguish imself above di presidents and di satraps, because excellent spirit dey inside am. Di king think to set am over di whole realm.
Den di presidents and di satraps seek to find occasion against Daniel concerning di kingdom, but dem no fit find any occasion or fault, because e dey faithful. No error or fault dey found for am.
Den dis men talk, “We no go find any occasion against dis Daniel, except we find am against am concerning di law of im God.”
Den dis presidents and satraps assemble together to di king, and talk like dis to am: “King Darius, live forever.

All di presidents of di kingdom, di deputies and di satraps, di counselors and di governors, don consult together to establish royal statute, and to make strong decree, say whoever go ask petition of any god or man for 30 days, except of you, king, go dey cast into di den of lions.
Now, king, establish di decree, and sign di writing, so that e no go dey changed, according to di law of di Medes and Persians, wey no dey pass away.”
Therefore King Darius sign di writing and di decree.

When Daniel know say di writing dey signed, e go into im house (now im windows dey open for im room toward Jerusalem). E kneel upon im knees three times for day, and pray, and give thanks before im God, as e do before.
Den dis men assemble together, and find Daniel making petition and supplication before im God.

Den dem come near, and speak before di king concerning di king decree: “You no sign decree say every man wey ask petition of any god or man within 30 days, except of you, king, go dey cast into di den of lions?” Di king answer, “Di thing dey true, according to di law of di Medes and Persians, wey no dey pass away.”
Den dem answer, and talk before di king, “Daniel, wey be one of di captives of Judah, no pay attention to you, king, nor to di decree wey you don sign, but make im petition three times for day.”
Den di king, when e hear dis words, dey very displeased, and set im heart on Daniel to deliver am. E labour till di going down of di sun to rescue am.
Den dis men assemble together to di king, and talk to di king, “Know, king, say na law of di Medes and Persians say no decree nor statute wey di king establish fit dey changed.”
Den di king command, and dem bring Daniel, and cast am into di den of lions. Now di king speak and talk to Daniel, “Your God whom you serve continually, e go deliver you.”
Dem bring stone, and lay am upon di mouth of di den. Di king seal am with im own signet, and with di signet of im lords, so that nothing no go change concerning Daniel.
Den di king go to im palace, and spend di night fasting. Neither dem bring instruments of music before am, and im sleep go from am.
Den di king rise very early for di morning, and go in haste to di den of lions.

When e come near to di den to Daniel, e cry with troubled voice. Di king speak and talk to Daniel, “Daniel, servant of di living God, your God, whom you serve continually, e don fit deliver you from di lions?”
Den Daniel talk to di king, “King, live forever.
My God don send im angel, and don shut di lions mouths, and dem no hurt me, because innocence dey found for me before am. Also before you, king, I don do no harm.”
Den di king dey exceeding glad for am, and command say dem go take Daniel up out of di den. So Daniel dey taken up out of di den, and no manner of hurt dey found upon am, because e trust for im God.

Di king command, and dem bring dem men wey don accuse Daniel, and dem cast dem into di den of lions, dem, dem children, and dem wives. Before dem reach di bottom of di den, di lions overpower dem, and break all dem bones in pieces.
Den King Darius write to all di peoples, nations, and languages wey dwell for all di earth: “Peace dey multiply to una.

I make decree say for all di dominion of my kingdom men go tremble and fear before di God of Daniel, because e na di living God, and steadfast forever. Im kingdom na di one wey no go dey destroyed, and im dominion go be even to di end.
E deliver and rescue, and e work signs and wonders for heaven and for earth, wey don deliver Daniel from di power of di lions.”
So dis Daniel prosper for di reign of Darius, and for di reign of Cyrus di Persian.
For di first year of Belshazzar king of Babylon Daniel get dream and visions of im head upon im bed. Den e write di dream and tell di sum of di matters.
Daniel speak and talk, “I see for my vision by night, and see, di four winds of heaven strive on di great sea.
Four great animals come up from di sea, diverse one from another.
Di first dey like lion, and get eagle wings. I watch until im wings dey plucked, and e dey lifted up from di earth, and make stand on im feet like man, and man heart dey given to am.
See, another animal, second, like bear. E dey raised up on one side, and e get three ribs for im mouth between im teeth. Dem talk like dis to am: ‘Arise, devour much flesh.’
After dis I look, and see another, like leopard, wey get on im back four wings of bird. Di animal get also four heads, and dominion dey given to am.

After dis I see for di night visions, and see, fourth animal, terrible and dreadful, and strong exceedingly. E get great iron teeth. E devour and break in pieces, and stamp di residue with im feet. E dey different from all di animals wey dey before am, and e get ten horns.

I consider di horns, and see, another horn, little one, come up among dem, and three of di first horns dey plucked up by di roots before am. See, for dis horn dey eyes like di eyes of man, and mouth speaking great things.
I watch until thrones dey placed, and one wey dey ancient of days sit. Im clothing dey white as snow, and di hair of im head like pure wool. Im throne dey fiery flames, and im wheels burning fire.
Stream of fire issue and come out from before am. Thousands upon thousands dey minister to am, and 10,000 times 10,000 dey stand before am. Di judgment dey set, and di books dey opened.
Den I watch because of di voice of di great words wey di horn dey speak. I watch even till di animal dey killed, and im body destroyed, and dem give am to di burning flame.
As for di rest of di animals, dem dominion dey taken away, but dem lives dey prolonged for season and time.
I see for di night visions, and see, one like son of man come with di clouds of heaven. E come even to di Ancient of Days, and dem bring am near before am.

Dominion dey given to am, and glory, and kingdom, so that all peoples, nations, and languages go serve am. Im dominion na everlasting dominion, wey no go pass away, and im kingdom na one wey no go dey destroyed.
As for me, Daniel, my spirit dey grieved inside my body, and di visions of my head trouble me.
I come near to one of dem wey stand by, and ask am di truth of all dis. So e tell me, and make me know di interpretation of di things:
‘Dis great animals, wey be four, na four kings, wey go arise out of di earth.
But di saints of di Most High go receive di kingdom, and possess di kingdom forever, even forever and ever.’

Den I desire to know di truth concerning di fourth animal, wey dey different from all di others, exceeding terrible, whose teeth dey iron and whose nails dey bronze, wey devour, break in pieces, and stamp di residue with im feet,

and concerning di ten horns wey dey on im head, and di other horn wey come up, and before am three fall, even dat horn wey get eyes, and mouth wey speak great things, whose look dey more stout pass im fellows.
I watch, and di same horn make war with di saints, and prevail against dem,
until di Ancient of Days come, and judgment dey given to di saints of di Most High, and di time come say di saints possess di kingdom.
Dis na wetin e talk: ‘Di fourth animal go be fourth kingdom upon earth, wey go dey different from all di kingdoms, and go devour di whole earth, and go tread am down, and break am in pieces.
As for di ten horns, out of dis kingdom ten kings go arise. Another go arise after dem. E go dey different from di former ones, and e go subdue three kings.
E go speak words against di Most High, and go wear out di saints of di Most High. E go think to change di times and di law, and dem go dey given into im hand until time and times and half time.
But di judgment go sit, and dem go take away im dominion, to consume and to destroy am to di end.

Di kingdom and di dominion, and di greatness of di kingdoms under di whole heaven, go dey given to di people of di saints of di Most High. Im kingdom na everlasting kingdom, and all dominions go serve and obey am.’
Here na di end of di matter. As for me, Daniel, my thoughts trouble me much, and my face change for me, but I keep di matter for my heart.”
